title: tool-calling: improve execution ergonomics for parallel multi-tool calls, result injection and retries
author: Ava Patel
description:
Context: multiple customers hit correctness and latency issues when using multi-tool tool-calling patterns with parallel tool invocations + result injection. We observed: (1) race conditions where injected tool results arrived after the model prompt was already continued (stale context), (2) unclear retry semantics when a downstream tool fails mid-parallel batch, and (3) streaming interruptions when tool results were injected into an in-progress stream.

This PR improves execution ergonomics for tool-calling in three areas: (A) parallel multi-tool coordination, (B) deterministic tool-result injection into model context (including streaming), and (C) a safe, idempotent retry policy for failed tool invocations. The high-level design and motivation are included below.

Design/Changes:
- Execution coordinator: add a lightweight per-request coordinator that tracks parallel tool invocations and guarantees deterministic ordering of injected results when requested by the prompt. The coordinator exposes tunables: injection_strategy (append | labeled-inline | placeholder-replace), ordering (first-completed | original-order | deterministic-by-name), and wait_timeout.
- Injection semantics: implement a new injection envelope that includes an "injection_id" and a stable placement marker. This lets the runtime inject results into ongoing streaming responses without breaking the chunking/state machine in the streaming layer. We also add explicit API flags so callers can request streaming-safe injection.
- Retry and idempotency: introduce idempotency tokens for tool invocations spawned from the same LLM request. Retries use exponential backoff with a bounded attempts config; failures are surfaced to the model as structured tool-error objects if retries exhaust. Retries are per-tool; failed tool retries do not implicitly cancel other parallel tools.
- Backcompat/OpenAI compatibility: the OpenAI-compat layer preserves previous defaults (no-wait injection_strategy, original-order) but exposes the new flags via the existing tools=[]/function_call fields to remain wire-compatible. Documented behavior changes are additive and opt-in for most callers.
- Streaming stability: streaming path updated to buffer partial injection events and interleave them with token chunks using the injection envelope; this avoids mid-stream parser breakage and improves client SDK resilience.

Files/areas changed (high level):
- runtime/toolcoord/executor.go: new coordinator + retry driver (major logic).
- runtime/streaming/injector.go: streaming-safe injection envelope and interleaving logic.
- api/openai_compat/tool_adapter.go: compatibility flags and mapping to new runtime controls.
- sdk/js/src/tooling.ts: helper types and examples for injection_strategy and retry config.
- docs/tool-calling.md: updated examples and rollout notes.
- e2e tests/tool-calling/parallel-injection.test.ts: new test harness covering ordering, retries, and streaming.

Commits summary: ["coord: add execution coordinator for parallel tool calls", "runtime: add idempotency tokens and retry driver", "streaming: implement injection envelope and interleaving", "openai-compat: map legacy function_call->injection flags", "sdk: expose injectionStrategy & retry config + examples", "tests: e2e and unit coverage for parallel tool calls"].

Rationale: customers commonly invoke multiple complementary tools (search, code-exec, external APIs) in parallel and expect deterministic behavior when results feed back into the model. Previously, teams either blocked serially (higher latency) or accepted nondeterministic continuation. This change provides opt-in semantics that let product teams choose correctness vs latency tradeoffs, while making the default behavior stable and safe for streaming use.

Testing and metrics: added unit tests + e2e that simulate slow/fast tool responses and mid-flight failures. We validated on internal perf lab; median latency for a 3-tool parallel request increased by ~1–3ms due to coordination overhead while 95th percentile decreased when using deterministic ordering (fewer retries/clarifications). CI: all checks pass.

Rollout: feature gated behind runtime flag "tool_exec_v2" and OpenAI-compat feature flag "tools_exec_ergonomics". We will rollout to Canary -> Dedicated -> Hosted over 2 weeks, monitor tool-calling error rates, streamer errors, and end-to-end latency (ENG-2871).

Notes: this PR focuses on runtime and API ergonomics; follow-ups are planned for telemetry (per-injection tracing spans) and a higher-level SDK helper that builds idempotency tokens for common tool integrations.

review_comments: Diego Ramos (review): Please ensure the default retry attempts for external HTTP tools is conservative; we don't want to encourage heavy retry storms. Also please add a telemetry counter for retry attempts.
Author (Ava): Updated to 3 attempts by default and added telemetry counter 'tool.invocation.retries'. Added per-tool backoff jitter to avoid thundering herd.
Jin Park (review): The streaming interleaving looks correct, but can you add a small validation for mixed placeholder types so we don't accidentally clobber user content?
Author (Ava): Added validation in injector.go to reject ambiguous placeholder names and added unit tests (injector_test.go).
Leah Kim (approval): Verified e2e against slow-tool fixture and confirmed streaming parser no longer fails on injected events. Approving.
Omar Haddad (approval): API mapping for OpenAI-compat looks backwards compatible. Approving.
merge_summary: Squash merged by Ava Patel. Preserved commit authors, added release notes and rollout plan.
release_notes: Add execution coordinator and streaming-safe tool-result injection. New API flags: injection_strategy, ordering, wait_timeout, plus idempotency token for retries. Backwards-compatible via OpenAI-compat defaults.\n\nImpact: improves determinism and streaming stability for multi-tool calls; opt-in ergonomics flag for gradual rollout.
post_merge_actions: Enable feature flag 'tool_exec_v2' on Canary after 24h monitoring
Follow-up: telemetry spans and SDK helper (ENG-2950)
